lead.headline: Teaching in Swedish prisons is a practice of its own, study finds
lead.standfirst: Interviews with 14 adult educators in Swedish prisons show a pedagogy built on trust, responsibility and empowerment.
body: Prison education is not simply adult education delivered under constraints, the authors argue, but a practice of its own, shaped by institutional rules, security routines and students’ varied educational backgrounds, and aimed at the students’ holistic development. It is negotiated between care and control, autonomy and coercion, trust and vigilance.
lead.more: Adult education in Swedish prisons (International Journal of Lifelong Education).

know.headline: Agency board changes for Cedefop, Eurofound and EU-OSHA
know.standfirst: The Council replaced a member of Cedefop’s Management Board for Bulgaria (decision of 24 September).
body: It also replaced a member and an alternate for Denmark at Eurofound (9 October) and members for Estonia and Cyprus at EU-OSHA (1 October).
know.more: Board changes at Cedefop, Eurofound and EU-OSHA (Official Journal).

know.headline: In AI hub Montreal, young graduates weigh chances against fears
know.standfirst: Some students and newcomers expect new opportunities; others fear their skills will soon be outdated, Le Monde reports (subscription).
know.more: Montreal’s young graduates and AI (Le Monde, subscription).

know.headline: New apprenticeship policies in Cedefop’s 2025 timeline update
know.standfirst: First reported in the 2025 update by Cedefop and ReferNet, as summarised on Apprentix.
body: They include Denmark’s substantial reinforcement of VET and mandatory work experience, Greece’s 2025–2027 strategic plan for VET, lifelong learning and youth, Slovakia’s tertiary VET reinforcement and Slovenia’s programme document for development planning until 2033.
know.more: New apprenticeship policies in Cedefop’s 2025 timeline update.

know.headline: EU leaders and social partners meet at the Tripartite Social Summit
know.standfirst: The twice-yearly summit brought EU leaders and social partners together in Brussels on 14 October.
know.more: Tripartite Social Summit, 14 October: EU leaders and social partners.

know.headline: Nine VETNET papers from ECER 2026 mention Cedefop
know.standfirst: Published on 13 October in the VETNET Conference Series.
body: They include studies of AI-mediated vocational pedagogy, embodied AI role-play in extended reality for retail apprentices, and an inclusive VET ecosystem.
know.more: Nine VETNET conference papers mention Cedefop.

know.headline: Vienna debates how young people find a way into apprenticeships
know.standfirst: At the Tag der Wiener Jugend, experts discussed the difficult search for apprenticeships and the falling number of training companies, Der Standard reports.
body: The head of Austria’s public employment service, AMS, told the event he is interested in applicants who have changed course.
know.more: Vienna: experts on young people’s hard search for apprenticeships (Der Standard).

lives.headline: Germany’s first carpentry world champion, 1967, still in the workshop at 78
lives.standfirst: He won gold at the forerunner of WorldSkills in Madrid at 18, ran the family firm for decades and trained most of its staff himself.
body: Albert Baumann grew up in a carpentry firm in Flein that his grandfather founded in 1896; as a child, he says, he was already working with a fretsaw. He began his apprenticeship in the family firm in 1964 and finished first at every level of the trade competitions, from guild to chamber to state. In 1966 he flew for the first time, to the national final in Berlin, his big carpenter’s saw stowed behind the back row on the airport staff’s advice. He won there too, at 18, and was honoured by the Federal President.

In July 1967 the German team went by coach from Duisburg to Madrid for the 16th International Vocational Training Competition, the forerunner of WorldSkills. The task was a hipped roof for a building with an extension, in three days. He finished first, after two, and used the spare time for sightseeing; he still talks about the Prado. On 17 July he took gold, ahead of young carpenters from Korea, the Netherlands, Ireland, Japan, Great Britain and Switzerland. Back in Flein, he recalls, customers came by to congratulate him, and some joked that prices would now go up, with a world champion in the workshop.

He qualified as a master carpenter in 1970 and took over the business from his father three years later. At its peak it employed twelve people, most of whom he had trained himself, and for decades he volunteered for the trade’s young people in the local carpenters’ guild. In 2012 he handed the firm to his children, the fourth generation. At 78 he still works in the workshop. Since 1967, four more German carpenters have won world gold, in 1973, 2003, 2015 and 2019.
